item.title: Canada's 2023 wildfires broke longstanding media caution around climate reporting
item.description: Fueled by record-breaking drought and unusually high temperatures, Canada's 2023 wildfire season was the worst in the country's history, with more than 15 million hectares (37 million acres) charred. item.description: En la provincia del Lago Chad, el cambio climático está alterando las condiciones de vida de comunidades que durante generaciones han dependido de sus aguas. item.title: How the moon and sun may trigger slow earthquakes on Earth
item.description: While not quite a fatal attraction, the gravitational pull of the moon and sun creates tiny stresses on Earth that can trigger events known as slow earthquakes. These are movements along fault lines (fault slips) that release their energy gradually over much longer periods than ordinary quakes. Although they have been observed, exactly how these celestial bodies trigger them has been a relatively tough nut to crack. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In 2002, a 3.5km sea wall was breached in five places at a 283-hectare Essex arable farm
item.description: In October 2002, a sea wall breach in Essex transformed farmland into a coastal wetland, increasing saltmarsh areas. This project, supported by various environmental organizations, aimed to restore natural habitats and manage coastal erosion. Marine life flourished, and biodiversity increased rapidly in the newly flooded areas after the breach. Traditional farming on higher land continued alongside saltmarsh restoration, contributing to sustainable agriculture. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
